nodes.description: Systemic antibiotics, or tetracycline, penicillin or chlorhexidine rinses, improve the lesions in some patients. Responses are inconsistent, lesions recur when treatment stops, and treatment does not alter the underlying disorder; long-term low-dose therapy has maintained remission in responders.

evidence.snippet: Four responded as judged by clinical examination, although not the 6-year-old female or the 18-month-old male; the discontinuation of therapy then resulted in clinical recurrence in those who had responded, but long-term low dose treatment maintained the remission.

nodes.description: A heterozygous variant in KRT4 or KRT13, usually a missense change or small in-frame indel in a helix boundary motif of the rod domain (most often the 1A helix initiation region of K13). These motifs are critical for keratin filament stability, so the mutant subunit acts on the network assembled by the wild-type allele. K4 and K13 are the major differentiation-specific keratin pair of buccal, nasal, esophageal and anogenital epithelia, which predicts the tissue distribution of the disease.

evidence.snippet: The mutation occurred within the conserved 1A region of the helical rod domain, which is critical for KIF stability and is the site of most pathogenic keratin mutations.
